newsitem.title: USA: U S West Media, Airtouch in definitive deal.
newsitem.headline: U S West Media, Airtouch in definitive deal.

text.p: AirTouch Communications Inc. has a definitive agreement to acquire U S West Media Group's cellular telephone operations in a deal valued at $5 billion, the companies said Friday.
Under the agreement announced in April, AirTouch will assume $2.2 billion in U S West Media debt and offer $2.8 billion of its shares to U S West Media shareholders.

In a new twist, however, U S West will now transfer its domestic phone directory business from U S West Media Group to U S West Communications Group. The two separately traded entities form U S West, the Englewood, Colo.-based regional phone company created by the breakup of AT&T Corp. in 1984.
For the U S West Dex directory business, U S West Communications will pay $850 million in stock to the Media group and assume $3.9 billion of debt.
This means that U S West Media shareholders will get four U S West Communications shares and 15 AirTouch shares for every 100 U S West Media shares, according to a U S West spokeswoman.
The agreement calls for AirTouch to issue between 84.8 million and 93.3 million shares to the media group, depending on AirTouch's share price.
AirTouch was unchanged at $25.75 on the New York Stock Exchange in late trading. U S West Communications dropped 12.5 cents to $34.875, while U S West Media rose 62.5 cents to $19, also on the NYSE.

After the deal closes, U S West Media's debt will fall to $3.9 billion from $10 billion. U S West Communications' debt will climb to $10.3 billion from $6.4 billion, but it will now benefit from the substantial cash flows generated by directory sales.
U S West Dex had revenues of just under $1 billion in 1996, the spokeswoman said.
Prudential Securities praised the move to integrate U S West's white and yellow pages directories business into the U S West phone unit instead its Media business.
Prudential cable TV analyst Melissa Cooke said her firm will continue to recommend the stock aggressively as a result of the deal.
"(U S West Media) had a choice of keeping the free cash flow of the directories business, or focusing on its core compentencies in the cable and wireless fields," Cooke said.
"Management is committed to simplification. It chose to focus on core growth businesses," she said.

"The logic is strong," agreed Prudential's telecom analyst Guy Woodlief, noting how sales of phone services would likely benefit from the intimate contact that the directories' sales force has with small- and medium-sized business customers.

This should provide a boost to U S West Communications as it seeks to enter the long-distance phone business as well as defend its existing 14-state local phone territory against incursions by competing service providers, Woodlief said.

U S West Communications provides telecommunications services in 14 Western and Midwestern states. It was set up in 1995 as a separately traded entity so that investors could track U S West's traditional telephone business separately from the wireless and cable TV interests in the Media Group.
U S West Media Group has operations in domestic and international cable and telephone service, wireless communications and directory and information services.
AirTouch, based in San Franciso, is a global wireless communications company, with interests in cellular, paging, and the newer personal communications services in the United States, Europe and Asia.
Under terms of its deal with U S West Media, AirTouch would obtain U S West Media Group's domestic wireless business and U S West Media would obtain an equity stake in AirTouch.
The proposed merger is subject to the companies' obtaining a ruling from the U.S. government granting tax-free status for the sale of U S West's wireless operations to AirTouch.
The companies said if they fail to obtain tax-free status, they will continue with a joint operating agreement established in 1994.
